question: Which of the following diseases is a potential contender for worldwide eradication?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Polio.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Smallpox is the only human disease to have been fully eradicated so far (WHO declared it eradicated in 1980). Polio is widely regarded as the next disease with a realistic chance of worldwide eradication. (पोलियो — वैश्विक उन्मूलन का प्रयास)

 

• The Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI), launched in 1988, has reduced polio cases by over 99% worldwide through mass immunisation with the oral polio vaccine (OPV).

 

• As of the recent past, wild poliovirus transmission has been restricted to only a couple of countries (Afghanistan and Pakistan), making it the disease closest to a second global eradication.

 

• Eradication requires interruption of person-to-person transmission everywhere, which is achievable for polio because humans are its only reservoir and an effective vaccine exists.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guinea worm disease (Dracunculiasis) is another disease very close to eradication, being tackled through the Guinea Worm Eradication Programme led by The Carter Center.

 

• Measles elimination (not full eradication) is a regional WHO target in several parts of the world, but the disease remains far more widespread globally than polio.

 

NOTE

 

• Tuberculosis (Option 2): Still a leading infectious killer worldwide; no eradication is currently in sight despite the WHO's "End TB" strategy.

 

• Measles (Option 3): Elimination (not global eradication) is targeted in specific WHO regions; the disease still causes large outbreaks globally.

 

• Malaria (Option 4): Remains endemic in large parts of Africa and Asia; despite the RTS,S vaccine rollout, global eradication is not imminent.

question: How many Gold medals India won in the Olympics between 1928 and 1980?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Between 1928 and 1980, India's men's hockey team won 8 Olympic gold medals. (भारतीय हॉकी — 8 स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• The gold-medal-winning years were: 1928 (Amsterdam), 1932 (Los Angeles), 1936 (Berlin), 1948 (London), 1952 (Helsinki), 1956 (Melbourne), 1964 (Tokyo), and 1980 (Moscow).

 

• India also won a silver in 1960 (Rome) and bronze medals in 1968 (Mexico City) and 1972 (Munich) during this dominant era of Indian hockey.

 

• This period is often called the 'Golden Era of Indian Hockey', with legends like Dhyan Chand and Balbir Singh Sr. leading India's dominance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first Olympic hockey gold came in 1928 at Amsterdam, its first appearance in Olympic hockey.

 

• The 1980 Moscow gold was India's last hockey gold for over four decades; India next won an Olympic hockey medal (bronze) at Tokyo 2020 (held in 2021) and again at Paris 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (7, 5, 6) all undercount India's total of 8 Olympic hockey gold medals won in this period.

question: Due to which of the following reasons can money be differentiated from other physical assets that can perform the function of store of value?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Money is easy to store.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Money performs the function of a store of value, allowing wealth to be held over time. (मुद्रा — मूल्य के भंडार का कार्य)

 

• Unlike other physical assets that can also serve as a store of value — such as land, buildings, gold and jewellery — holding wealth as money is far easier to store, since it needs no special safekeeping arrangements, incurs no maintenance or depreciation cost, and does not require physical upkeep the way land or valuables do.

 

• This ease of storage, along with money's convenience for later use, is a key reason it is preferred over holding wealth in the form of bulky or perishable physical assets.

 

• Money's general/common acceptability (Option 1) is what makes it a good medium of exchange, a separate function from its role as a store of value.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four traditional functions of money are: medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account, and standard of deferred payment.

 

• Money is also considered the most liquid asset, meaning it can be readily used for transactions without conversion cost — a related but distinct advantage from ease of storage.

 

NOTE

 

• Money has common acceptability (Option 1): This describes money's role as a medium of exchange, not what differentiates it as a store of value from other physical assets.

 

• Money possesses liquidity (Option 2): Liquidity is a related property of money but is not the specific reason contrasting it with the storage difficulty of physical assets like land or gold.

 

• Money is neutral (Option 3): 'Neutrality of money' is a macroeconomic theory (about money not affecting real variables), unrelated to the store-of-value comparison being asked about here.

question: English as the official language of India for higher education was incorporated in the resolution formulation by ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Macaulay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Macaulay's Minute on Indian Education (2 February 1835) argued for making English the medium of instruction for higher education in India, rather than Sanskrit, Persian or Arabic. (मैकाले का शिक्षा प्रस्ताव — 1835)

 

• Macaulay's recommendations were formally adopted through the English Education Act, 1835, passed under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck, which incorporated English as the official language for higher/government-funded education.

 

• Macaulay famously argued that a class of Indians 'Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste' should be created through English education.

 

• This decision profoundly shaped the subsequent development of Western-style education and the English language's spread in colonial India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wood's Despatch (1854), issued by Sir Charles Wood, is called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India' and laid down a comprehensive framework for education, including the creation of universities.

 

• The Hunter Commission (1882) later reviewed the progress of the Wood's Despatch recommendations.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Hastings (Option 1): As Governor-General (1813-1823), he promoted indigenous education and helped establish the Hindu College, Calcutta (1817), but did not author the English-medium resolution.

 

• Lord Wellesley (Option 2): Founded the Fort William College (1800) for training British civil servants, unrelated to Macaulay's Minute.

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 4): Known for the Doctrine of Lapse, and for introducing railways, telegraph and postal reforms; Wood's Despatch of 1854 was issued during his tenure but was not authored by him.

question: Who was the author of the book 'Vrihat Katha Kosha'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harisena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Brihatkathakosha' (Vrihat Katha Kosha) was composed by Harisena, a Digambara Jain monk, in 931 CE. (बृहत्कथाकोश — हरिषेण)

 

• It is a Sanskrit prose collection of moral and religious stories illustrating Jain doctrine, meant to popularise Jain teachings among common people.

 

• It is considered an important source of medieval Jain literature and social history of the period.

 

• The title literally means 'The Great Collection of Stories', continuing the tradition of the older, now-lost Brihatkatha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original Brihatkatha was composed by Gunadhya in the Paishachi language; the text itself is lost but survives through later Sanskrit adaptations.

 

• Two major surviving adaptations of Gunadhya's Brihatkatha are the Kathasaritsagara by Somadeva and the Brihatkathamanjari by Kshemendra, both from the 11th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Laxmidhar (Option 1): Author of the Krityakalpataru, a medieval digest (Nibandha) on Hindu law and rituals.

 

• Jayanaka (Option 2): Author of Prithviraja Vijaya, a Sanskrit epic on Prithviraj Chauhan III.

 

• Rajashekhar (Option 4): A 9th-10th century poet-playwright known for works like Kavyamimamsa and Karpuramanjari.

question: Which of these is NOT the reason why 'final' goods are called so?
option_1: They are meant for final use.
option_2: They are the last to be consumed.
option_3: They will not pass through any more stages of production.
option_4: They are not processed or transformed further.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are the last to be consumed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Final goods are goods that are meant either for final consumption or for investment (capital formation), and do not undergo any further stage of production or transformation. (अंतिम वस्तुएं — उत्पादन की अंतिम अवस्था)

 

• The correct defining features of final goods are that they are meant for final use, will not pass through any more stages of production, and are not further processed or transformed.

 

• Calling them 'the last to be consumed' is inaccurate as the sole defining reason, because final goods also include capital/investment goods (like machinery bought by a firm), which are not 'consumed' in the everyday sense at all — they are used for further production, yet still count as final goods since they leave the production boundary.

 

• Hence, describing final goods purely in terms of being 'last to be consumed' is not the correct or complete reason behind the terminology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Final goods are contrasted with intermediate goods, which are used up as raw material/inputs in producing other goods within the same accounting year.

 

• Correctly classifying goods as final or intermediate is essential to avoid the problem of double counting while calculating national income (GDP).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 are all standard, textbook-correct reasons for why goods are termed 'final' — they are meant for final use, do not pass through further stages of production, and are not processed or transformed further.

question: Which city in India is known as the 'Detroit of India' due to its automobile industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chennai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chennai, Tamil Nadu, is popularly called the 'Detroit of India' because of its large concentration of automobile and auto-component manufacturing units. (चेन्नई — भारत का डेट्रॉइट)

 

• Major automakers with plants near Chennai include Ford, Hyundai, Renault-Nissan, Ashok Leyland, BMW, Daimler (Mercedes-Benz), and Royal Enfield, among others.

 

• The city and its surrounding industrial belt (including Sriperumbudur and Oragadam) account for a substantial share of India's automobile production and exports.

 

• The name is derived by analogy with Detroit, Michigan (USA), historically the hub of the American automobile industry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Detroit, USA is known as 'Motor City', home to major American automakers like General Motors, Ford and Chrysler (Stellantis).

 

• Chennai is also called the 'Gateway of South India' due to its major port and connectivity role.

 

NOTE

 

• Mumbai (Option 2): Known as India's financial and entertainment (Bollywood) capital.

 

• Bengaluru (Option 3): Known as the 'Silicon Valley of India', the hub of India's IT industry.

 

• Pune (Option 4): Also has a significant automobile industry (in Pimpri-Chinchwad), but the title 'Detroit of India' is specifically and popularly associated with Chennai.

question: In which year did RBI introduce the regulatory framework for microfinance loans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued the 'Master Direction - Reserve Bank of India (Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans) Directions, 2022' on 14 March 2022, effective from 1 April 2022. (माइक्रोफाइनेंस ऋण नियामक ढांचा — 2022)

 

• This framework harmonised regulations for all regulated entities (banks, NBFC-MFIs, etc.) offering microfinance loans, replacing the earlier NBFC-MFI-specific rules.

 

• It removed the interest rate cap for NBFC-MFIs (subject to a board-approved policy) and introduced a household income-based cap on total loan repayment obligations.

 

• The framework also mandated increased transparency in pricing and prohibited pre-payment penalties on microfinance loans.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A microfinance loan under this framework is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household with annual income up to ₹3 lakh.

 

• The framework aims to protect vulnerable borrowers from over-indebtedness and predatory lending practices.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (2021, 2020, 2019) are incorrect years — the current regulatory framework for microfinance loans was notified by the RBI in 2022.

question: Who among the following won the bronze medal at the World Under-20 Wrestling championship 2022, which was held at Sofia, Bulgaria?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohit Dahiya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The World Under-20 (Junior) Wrestling Championships 2022 were held at Sofia, Bulgaria in August 2022, where Indian wrestlers had a record-breaking campaign. (विश्व अंडर-20 कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप 2022 — सोफिया, बुल्गारिया)

 

• India won a record 16 medals at this edition across freestyle, women's freestyle and Greco-Roman categories.

 

• Among the Indian contingent representing the country at this Under-20 event, Rohit Dahiya was among the wrestlers selected and won a bronze medal.

 

• This event was notable for Antim Panghal becoming India's first-ever U20 World Champion in wrestling (gold medal).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Under-20 category is also referred to as the 'Junior' category in international wrestling.

 

• India's overall strong showing at this event reflected the growing depth of junior-level wrestling talent in the country.

 

NOTE

 

• Bajrang Punia (Option 4): A senior-level Olympic and World Championship medallist wrestler; he did not compete in this Under-20 (junior) event, making this option a clear distractor.

 

• Atul Malhotra and Vikas Khedkar (Options 1 and 2): Not the wrestlers credited with this particular bronze medal at the 2022 World U20 Championships.

question: The provision for the post of Vice-President in the Indian Constitution was taken from ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is United States of America.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The office of the Vice-President of India (Articles 63-71 of the Constitution) was borrowed from the United States of America, which also has the analogous post of Vice-President. (उपराष्ट्रपति पद — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका)

 

• Like the American Vice-President, the Indian Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

 

• The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament, through proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.

 

• Other features India borrowed from the USA's Constitution include Fundamental Rights, judicial review, the independence of the judiciary, and the procedure of impeachment of the President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's Constitution is often called a 'bag of borrowings' since it draws features from various countries while adapting them to Indian conditions.

 

• From Ireland, India borrowed the Directive Principles of State Policy and the method of the President's election.

 

NOTE

 

• France (Option 1): India borrowed the ideals of Liberty, Equality, Fraternity (from the French Revolution) and the concept of a Republic, not the Vice-President's office.

 

• Ireland (Option 3): Source of the Directive Principles of State Policy and the nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha, not the Vice-Presidency.

 

• Japan (Option 4): India borrowed the concept of 'procedure established by law' (Article 21) from Japan.

question: Which of the following Indian pairs won the gold medal in Badminton in Commonwealth Games -2022 held in August 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, the Indian men's doubles badminton pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty won the gold medal. (सात्विकसाईराज-चिराग शेट्टी — बैडमिंटन स्वर्ण, सीडब्ल्यूजी 2022)

 

• This pairing, popularly known as 'Satchi', defeated Malaysia's pair in the final to claim the gold in men's doubles.

 

• The Commonwealth Games 2022 were held in Birmingham, England, from 28 July to 8 August 2022.

 

• India's badminton contingent had a highly successful campaign at this edition, winning multiple medals across singles and doubles events.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lakshya Sen won the gold medal in men's singles badminton at CWG 2022.

 

• P. V. Sindhu won the gold medal in women's singles badminton at the same Games.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 each pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, Chirag Shetty, or Srikanth Kidambi incorrectly with Lakshya Sen, who won his gold in the singles event, not doubles.

question: According to the Köppen classification, which letter code represents a tropical climate with a dry winter season found in large parts of peninsular India south of the Tropic of Cancer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aw.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Köppen climate classification, the code 'Aw' denotes the Tropical Savanna (wet and dry) climate, characterised by a distinct dry winter season. (कोपेन जलवायु वर्गीकरण — Aw उष्णकटिबंधीय सवाना)

 

• This climate type covers large parts of peninsular India, especially the Deccan Plateau region south of the Tropic of Cancer, including much of Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu's interior.

 

• In Köppen's system, 'A' stands for tropical climates (coldest month above 18°C), and 'w' denotes a dry-winter regime, distinguishing it from the fully humid tropical monsoon climate.

 

• Areas with Aw climate typically receive concentrated rainfall during the southwest monsoon, followed by a pronounced dry season in winter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 'Am' represents the Tropical Monsoon climate, found along India's west coast (e.g., Konkan, Malabar).

 

• 'BWh'/'BWk' represent hot/cold desert climates, found in western Rajasthan.

 

NOTE

 

• BWk (Option 1): Denotes a cold desert climate, not applicable to peninsular tropical India.

 

• CWh (Option 3): Not the code typically used for peninsular India in this classification scheme.

 

• Dw (Option 4): Denotes a cold, continental climate with dry winters, found in temperate/high-latitude regions, not applicable to India.

question: In 2022, Chief Minister MK Stalin introduced the 'Pudhumai Penn' (Modern women) programme, under which all female students enrolled in government schools from classes 6 through 12 will receive ________ each month to pursue higher education.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹1,000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M. K. Stalin launched the 'Pudhumai Penn' (meaning 'Modern/New Woman') scheme, providing ₹1,000 per month (₹12,000 per year) to girl students studying in government and government-aided schools from Class 6 to Class 12. (पुधुमई पेन योजना — तमिलनाडु, ₹1,000/माह)

 

• The scheme aims to prevent school dropouts among girls and encourage them to pursue higher education after Class 12.

 

• The amount is transferred through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) directly into the student's own bank account.

 

• The scheme is implemented by the Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, Government of Tamil Nadu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pudhumai Penn was launched building on the earlier 'Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme' for girl students.

 

• The scheme forms part of Tamil Nadu's broader efforts to improve the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of girls in higher education.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (₹2,000, ₹2,500, ₹1,500) are incorrect amounts; the scheme provides ₹1,000 per month to eligible girl students.

question: Which of the following is a traditional dance form of Sri Lanka?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kandyan dance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kandyan dance is a traditional and classical dance form of Sri Lanka, originating in the hill city of Kandy, the seat of the last Sinhalese kingdom. (कैंडियन नृत्य — श्रीलंका)

 

• It is characterised by vigorous, acrobatic movements, elaborate costumes, and is traditionally accompanied by the Geta Beraya drum.

 

• Kandyan dance comprises several sub-styles, and its most well-known form is the Ves dance, performed at the annual Esala Perahera festival in Kandy.

 

• It is recognised as one of the most iconic classical dance traditions of Sri Lanka, reflecting the island's rich cultural heritage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other traditional Sri Lankan dance forms include the Low Country (Pahatha Rata) dance and the Sabaragamuwa dance.

 

• Sri Lankan classical dance heavily influenced ritual and devil-dancing traditions of the island's southern and western coastal regions.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihu (Option 1): A folk dance associated with the Bihu festival of Assam, India.

 

• Kathak (Option 2): One of the eight classical dance forms of India, associated with North India.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 4): A classical dance form originating in Tamil Nadu, India.

question: Who among the following personalities is known as the 'Queen of Carnatic Music'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is MS Subbulakshmi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• M. S. Subbulakshmi is widely known as the 'Queen of Carnatic Music', celebrated for her mastery of Carnatic classical vocal music. (एम.एस. सुब्बुलक्ष्मी — कर्नाटक संगीत की रानी)

 

• She was the first musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 1998.

 

• She was also the first Indian to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1974), often called 'Asia's Nobel Prize'.

 

• Her renditions of devotional compositions like 'Suprabhatam' and 'Bhaja Govindam' remain iconic in Indian classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• M. S. Subbulakshmi famously performed at the United Nations General Assembly in 1966 to mark UN Day.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1954) and Padma Vibhushan (1975) prior to the Bharat Ratna.

 

NOTE

 

• Lata Mangeshkar (Option 4): Legendary Indian playback singer, referred to as the 'Nightingale of India', primarily associated with Hindustani/film music, not Carnatic music.

 

• Kavita Krishnamoorti and Vijaya Rajendran (Options 2 and 3): Not associated with the title 'Queen of Carnatic Music'.

question: Which of the following statements best describes the characteristics of a crystalline solid?
option_2: There is no precise melting point
option_4: Changes abruptly from solid to liquid when heated
solution_text:
The correct answer is Changes abruptly from solid to liquid when heated.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Crystalline solids have particles arranged in a highly ordered, repeating three-dimensional pattern called a lattice. (क्रिस्टलीय ठोस — निश्चित गलनांक)

 

• Because of this ordered structure, crystalline solids possess a sharp, definite (precise) melting point, and change abruptly from the solid to the liquid state when heated to that temperature.

 

• Examples of crystalline solids include sodium chloride (NaCl), diamond, quartz, and sugar (sucrose).

 

• Crystalline solids are also characterised by anisotropy (different physical properties in different directions) due to their ordered internal structure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amorphous (pseudo) solids, such as glass, rubber and plastic, lack long-range order and therefore soften gradually over a range of temperatures rather than melting sharply.

 

• Amorphous solids are also called 'super-cooled liquids' because of their disordered, liquid-like molecular arrangement.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (easily deforms, no precise melting point, uneven 3D layout) actually describe characteristics of amorphous solids, not crystalline solids.

question: Which of the following correctly represents the number of atoms in one mole of CH₃OH?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.6 × 10²⁴.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Methanol (CH₃OH) has the molecular formula CH₄O, containing 6 atoms per molecule (1 carbon + 4 hydrogen + 1 oxygen). (मेथेनॉल — एक मोल में परमाणुओं की संख्या)

 

• One mole of any substance contains Avogadro's number of entities, i.e., 6.022 × 10²³ molecules.

 

• Total number of atoms in one mole of CH₃OH = 6 atoms/molecule × 6.022 × 10²³ molecules ≈ 3.6 × 10²⁴ atoms.

 

• This calculation applies Avogadro's constant, a foundational concept for converting between moles, molecules, and atoms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹) is used universally to relate the amount of substance (in moles) to the actual number of particles.

 

• One mole of any gas at STP occupies 22.4 litres, another key mole-concept relationship.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (6.0 × 10²³): This is approximately Avogadro's number itself, i.e., the number of molecules, not atoms, in one mole of CH₃OH.

 

• Option 3 (3.0 × 10²⁵): An incorrect, overstated figure not matching the atom-count calculation.

 

• Option 4 (3): Far too small; does not correspond to any correct mole-based calculation.

question: Rann Utsav is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rann Utsav is an annual cultural festival held in the White (Great) Rann of Kutch, in the state of Gujarat. (रण उत्सव — गुजरात)

 

• It is typically organised from November to February, coinciding with the winter season and full moon nights over the salt desert.

 

• The festival is organised by the Gujarat Tourism Department, primarily centred around Dhordo village near the India-Pakistan border.

 

• It showcases Kutchi handicrafts, folk music and dance, cuisine, and camel/desert safaris, drawing large numbers of domestic and international tourists.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rann of Kutch is one of the largest salt deserts in the world, famous for its stark white landscape during the dry season.

 

• Gujarat also hosts other major cultural festivals like the Navratri Garba festival and the International Kite Festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa, Punjab and Haryana (Options 1, 2 and 4) are not associated with the Rann Utsav, which is uniquely tied to the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic questions every society needs to answer?
option_1: How should the goods be distributed?
option_3: What goods and services to produce?
option_4: How should the goods be exchanged?
solution_text:
The correct answer is How should the goods be exchanged?

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Every economy, due to the scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants, must answer three central/basic economic questions. (अर्थव्यवस्था की मूल समस्याएँ — वस्तु विनिमय नहीं)

 

• These are: (i) What to produce (what goods and services, and in what quantities), (ii) How to produce (which techniques/methods of production to use), and (iii) For whom to produce (how the goods should be distributed among members of society).

 

• 'How should the goods be distributed' corresponds to the 'for whom to produce' question, and 'how should goods be produced' corresponds directly to the 'how to produce' question.

 

• 'How should the goods be exchanged' is not one of these three classical central problems of an economy; exchange mechanisms are a separate economic consideration, not one of the foundational questions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• These central problems arise in every economic system — whether capitalist, socialist, or mixed — though each system answers them differently (via markets, central planning, or a combination).

 

• The Production Possibility Curve (PPC) is often used to illustrate the 'what to produce' problem given limited resources.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 each correctly represent one of the three standard central problems of an economy (distribution/for whom, how to produce, and what to produce respectively).

question: Which of the following is a feature of fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution ?
option_1: Some of them available to legal expertise.
option_3: Some of them are available to foreigners.
option_4: The Constitution does not provide for their direct enforcement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Constitution does not provide for their direct enforcement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Article 51A, added to Part IVA of the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — गैर-प्रवर्तनीय)

 

• A key feature of the Fundamental Duties is that they are non-justiciable — the Constitution does not provide any direct legal mechanism or sanction to enforce them against a citizen who fails to comply.

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, which are enforceable by courts, Fundamental Duties are essentially moral obligations meant to remind citizens of their responsibilities towards the nation.

 

• However, Parliament can indirectly enforce them by enacting laws that impose penalties for their non-compliance (e.g., laws related to protecting national symbols).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties — the original 10 added in 1976, plus 1 more added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 (duty of parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6-14 years).

 

• Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

NOTE

 

• Some of them available to legal expertise (Option 1): Not a recognised or accurate feature of Fundamental Duties.

 

• Reasonable restrictions can be imposed (Option 2): This concept applies to Fundamental Rights (e.g., under Article 19), not to Fundamental Duties.

 

• Some of them are available to foreigners (Option 3): Fundamental Duties under Article 51A apply only to citizens of India, not to foreigners.

question: Identify the true statement among the following.
option_1: Income Tax is an Indirect Tax
option_2: Goods and Services Tax is a direct tax
option_3: Fees and Fines collected is a non-tax receipt
option_4: Borrowings from the public is a revenue receipt
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fees and Fines collected is a non-tax receipt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Government revenue receipts are classified into Tax Revenue and Non-Tax Revenue. (शुल्क और जुर्माना — गैर-कर राजस्व)

 

• Fees and fines collected by the government (e.g., court fines, licence fees, registration fees) are examples of Non-Tax Revenue, since they are charges for specific services or penalties, not compulsory taxes.

 

• A tax is a compulsory payment with no direct quid-pro-quo (return service), whereas a fee is charged in return for a specific service rendered.

 

• This makes the statement about fees and fines being a non-tax receipt the correct/true statement among the given options.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of Non-Tax Revenue include interest receipts, dividends and profits from public sector undertakings (PSUs), and external grants.

 

• Revenue receipts (whether tax or non-tax) neither create a liability nor reduce an asset of the government, unlike capital receipts.

 

NOTE

 

• Income Tax is an Indirect Tax (Option 1): False — Income Tax is a Direct Tax, since its burden cannot be shifted to another person.

 

• Goods and Services Tax is a direct tax (Option 2): False — GST is an Indirect Tax, as its burden can be shifted from the seller to the buyer.

 

• Borrowings from the public is a revenue receipt (Option 4): False — Borrowings are a Capital Receipt, since they create a liability (debt) for the government that must be repaid.

question: The One Dance UK Lifetime Achievement Award 2021 in South Asian Dance was given to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Smita Vadnerkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Smita Vadnerkar, a UK-based Kathak dancer and choreographer, was honoured with the One Dance UK Lifetime Achievement Award for South Asian Dance in 2021. (वन डांस यूके जीवन उपलब्धि पुरस्कार 2021 — स्मिता वाडनेरकर)

 

• She is the founder and artistic director of the Smita Vadnerkar Dance Company (Nupur Arts), based in the UK.

 

• She has spent over three decades promoting and teaching Indian classical dance forms, mainly Kathak, in the United Kingdom.

 

• Her work spans choreography, training emerging dancers, and participation in international dance festivals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• One Dance UK is the national body supporting dance in the United Kingdom across genres, including its annual awards recognising outstanding contributions to the sector.

 

• South Asian dance in the UK diaspora has grown significantly, with organisations like Nupur Arts playing a key role in its promotion.

 

NOTE

 

• Maggie Morris, Alysha Kassam and Kamara Gray (Options 2, 3 and 4): Not associated with the 2021 One Dance UK Lifetime Achievement Award for South Asian Dance.

question: Which of the following is a folk dance from the state of Gujarat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tippani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tippani is a traditional folk dance of Gujarat, popular in the Saurashtra region. (टिप्पणी नृत्य — गुजरात)

 

• It is traditionally performed by women labourers, using long sticks called 'tippani' to rhythmically flatten and compact floors or roofs while singing and dancing.

 

• The dance blends functional labour with performance, reflecting the working traditions of rural Gujarati communities.

 

• It is performed in groups, with synchronised striking movements of the sticks on the ground, accompanied by folk songs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Gujarat include Garba and Dandiya Raas, both closely associated with the Navratri festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Phag (Option 2): A folk dance/song tradition associated with Holi celebrations, popular in the Braj region (Uttar Pradesh) and Rajasthan.

 

• Dhimsa (Option 3): A tribal folk dance of the Koraput region of Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Dhamal (Option 4): A folk/devotional dance associated with Sindh and Rajasthan/Sufi traditions, not Gujarat.

question: The Jog Falls, one of the highest waterfalls in India is the cataract of which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sharavati.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jog Falls, one of the highest waterfalls in India, is formed by the Sharavati River in the Shivamogga (Shimoga) district of Karnataka. (जोग जलप्रपात — शरावती नदी)

 

• It is also known as Gerusoppa Falls or Jogada Gundi, and has a height of approximately 253 metres (830 feet).

 

• The waterfall is segmented into four distinct cascades, popularly named Raja, Rani, Rocket, and Roarer.

 

• The Sharavati River is also harnessed for hydroelectric power generation at the Mahatma Gandhi Hydroelectric Station near the falls.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karnataka is home to several major waterfalls, including Shivanasamudra Falls on the Kaveri (Cauvery) river.

 

• The Sharavati river itself originates in the Western Ghats and flows westward into the Arabian Sea.

 

NOTE

 

• Narmada, Tungabhadra and Cauvery (Options 1, 2 and 4): These are other major rivers of India, but none of them form the Jog Falls.

question: Narayan Guru, a social reformer from Ezhava caste and who propagated an anti-caste movement, was born in which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sree Narayana Guru (1856-1928), a social reformer and spiritual leader from the Ezhava community, was born in Chempazhanthy, near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. (श्री नारायण गुरु — केरल)

 

• He founded the Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam in 1903 to uplift the socially backward classes of Kerala and campaign against caste-based discrimination.

 

• His famous teaching, 'Oru Jathi, Oru Matham, Oru Daivam Manushyanu' ('One Caste, One Religion, One God for Mankind'), became a rallying philosophy of the anti-caste movement in Kerala.

 

• He led the historic Aruvippuram consecration (1888), installing a Shiva idol as an act of defiance against caste restrictions on temple worship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sree Narayana Guru is also credited with pioneering the temple entry and social equality movements that influenced later reform efforts across Kerala.

 

• His philosophy significantly influenced Kerala's socio-political landscape and contributed to the state's later achievements in social development.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu (Options 1, 3 and 4): Incorrect states; Sree Narayana Guru was born and primarily active in Kerala.
